goal_text: I want to learn about AI

nodes.title: What is AI, really?
nodes.one_liner: Plain-language meaning behind the term everyone uses.

nodes.title: How does a machine "learn"?
nodes.one_liner: What training on data means, without the math.

nodes.title: What are ChatGPT and friends?
nodes.one_liner: How large language models work and why they impress.

nodes.title: The AI vocabulary decoder
nodes.one_liner: Model, neural net, GPT, token, hallucination, explained simply.

nodes.title: Where you already meet AI
nodes.one_liner: Everyday uses in phones, search, recommendations, images.

nodes.title: Why everyone's arguing about AI
nodes.one_liner: Jobs, bias, safety, copyright, and the big debates.

nodes.title: Who's building AI, and who's winning?
nodes.one_liner: The key companies, labs, and people in the news.

nodes.title: Reading AI headlines without panic
nodes.one_liner: Spotting hype, real progress, and misleading claims.

outline.rationale: The user is a total beginner whose sole goal is following AI news and conversing about it—understanding, not building. So I excluded any hands-on, coding, math, or tool-usage nodes. The outline builds from foundational meaning ("What is AI") through the mechanism ("how machines learn") to the specific technology dominating headlines (LLMs/ChatGPT), since that's what most news references. A vocabulary node directly serves the "decode headlines" goal. Everyday-uses grounds abstract concepts in familiar experience. The debates and players nodes cover the socio-political and industry context that fills most AI news. The final node is a media-literacy capstone that directly addresses "understand the news" by teaching hype detection—a payoff that depends on all prior nodes. Nodes are MECE-ish: definition, mechanism, flagship tech, terms, applications, controversies, actors, and critical reading each occupy distinct territory with low overlap.
